items.headline: DHS order bars DeepSeek products from federal civilian agencies
items.title: Notice of Order Regarding Exclusion and Removal of DeepSeek Products From Federal Civilian Executive Branch Information Technology Systems and Procurements
items.harder: Federal civilian agencies can no longer buy DeepSeek IT products and services and must remove them, along with third-party products built using DeepSeek implementations, from their systems.
items.quote: removing all DeepSeek and DeepSeek-affiliate products, and third-party products and services developed using DeepSeek implementations, from civilian agency information technology.
items.who: DeepSeek, its affiliates, and vendors whose products use DeepSeek
items.why: Vendors selling to US federal civilian agencies cannot ship products developed using DeepSeek implementations.
items.limits: effective date not stated in the notice

ripples.effect: DeepSeek models leave federal civilian agency IT systems
Vendors must trace DeepSeek components inside third-party products

hats.architect: Federal-facing products need a model layer that can drop DeepSeek implementations.
hats.quality: Test that replacement models meet the behavior previously delivered by DeepSeek components.
hats.security: Inventory dependencies for DeepSeek or DeepSeek-affiliate code before federal civilian deployments.
hats.product: DeepSeek-based features cannot be offered to federal civilian agency customers.
hats.scout: Watch for which affiliated entities the applicable regulations cover.

sources.name: Federal Register
sources.title: Notice of Order Regarding Exclusion and Removal of DeepSeek Products From Federal Civilian Executive Branch Information Technology Systems and Procurements

items.headline: EU publishes first AI Act harmonised standard for high-risk providers
items.title: First harmonised standard supporting the AI Act published in the Official Journal
items.harder: Providers of high-risk AI systems in the EU now have a defined operational quality management system to build or adopt in order to gain presumption of conformity with Article 17.
items.quote: Organisations without ISO/IEC 42001 that plan to place or put into service high-risk AI systems in the EU market can use EN 18286 to expand an existing QMS or build one that fulfills the requirements of article 17 requirements.
items.who: Providers of high-risk AI systems in the EU
items.why: Teams placing high-risk AI systems on the EU market now have a concrete QMS benchmark to meet.
items.limits: further harmonised standards still expected; high-risk requirements not yet applying

ripples.effect: Lifecycle QMS processes become the reference for high-risk compliance

hats.architect: Design high-risk AI system lifecycles to map onto EN 18286 QMS processes.
hats.quality: QMS processes mapped to Article 17 become the benchmark for high-risk systems.
hats.product: Budget QMS work before shipping high-risk AI systems into the EU market.
hats.scout: Watch for further harmonised standards supporting the AI Act.
hats.combinator: EN 18286 layers on ISO/IEC 42001, ISO 9001 or sectoral QMS like ISO 13485.

sources.name: European Commission: digital strategy (AI Act)
